answer: Resist sybils with physics, not trust. Credential ceremonies run worldwide in one hour; rooms publish signed attendance, and one body can stand in only one room, so each human can hold only the current epoch's umber badge — the only badge consensus pays. Hiring bodies costs a wage per identity, linear and parallel; cap each badge's reward below that wage, so farming k badges loses money. Bribed rooms and forged tapes remain: no ceremony is a haven without random video audits. The fable that account count equals people dies; wage-paying influence buyers still get through.
